items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: John Heard, the great bass player, he was in the union one time and then he quit because the union wasn’t doing anything for him.

ctx.x: So the players would have been in the union for the most part?

Right. I mean most of your good players were in the union. Jazz players were in the union, and then some, like I shouldn’t mention his name but I will because he’s gone now, but John Heard, the great bass player, he was in the union one time and then he quit because the union wasn’t doing anything for him. He never got into motion pictures or TV or anything, he was strictly jazz in the bars. So I tried, when I was president, I was trying to get agreements with the bar owners to have a low scale for them, like…

Yeah it’s the same here in Central New York for years. Most of the players are not full time musicians so the concept of getting a gig at a local club and then bringing up with the owner like, “Okay here’s my union contract,” that would just be something like, “what are you talking about?”
